analysis:
Reviewed the two head_text units from SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift (lines 1756-3038). The file is test-only; the only changed lines per file_changes are 3140-3240, which fall outside both units' visible range. The patch excerpt is truncated and shows only new tests for SSDWholeRootMaintainer. These tests check that header-ownership verdicts are remembered only for unchanged files (ctime-based) and that a replaced lookalike is re-read. If anything, they strengthen coverage of the T-041 mitigations (TTL/LRU sweep, whole-root maintenance, ownership proof before deletion).

The visible lines contain only pre-existing tests: ready receipts, write-barrier failure matrix, staging reservation release, root isolation, and whole-root maintenance. They touch no production code, so no change to keys, AAD, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, disk budgets, scope handling or coordinator-facing behavior is introduced. They also cover no new endpoints, secrets or trust boundaries.

Remaining question: the production change that these new tests exercise (the SSDWholeRootMaintainer header-verdict cache keyed on size, mtime and ctime) is not in the supplied units. A later pass should check that implementation for correctness, in particular that a cached 'not owned' or 'owned' verdict cannot let TTL or budget eviction delete non-cache files, or skip expiry of owned files. That is where T-041's at-rest purge guarantees would be affected. I flag no issue here because only test code is visible.
